Name: Castulo, Silver-Mining Hub of Andalusia: The Mountain City and the Barcid Vein of Wealth
RagShortTexts: Castulo is the chief stronghold of the Oretani and controls the vast silver mines of the Sierra Morena
Hannibal married Imilce, a princess of Castulo, sealing a royal marriage alliance and economic bond
Hundreds of pounds of pure silver a day paid the enormous wages of Carthage's hundreds of thousands of mercenaries
BaseText: Castulo (castle_carthage_castulo) stands on the heights of the north bank of the upper Guadalquivir, against the southern slopes of the mineral-rich Sierra Morena. It is the most powerful fortified city of the Iberian Oretani, and it directly controls the ancient silver mine of Baebelo, the richest in the entire Mediterranean world. According to Pliny, this one mine alone required thousands of slaves to work it every day and yielded more than three hundred pounds of pure silver daily. Hannibal's father Hamilcar and Hannibal himself knew that this place was the lifeblood of the war, and Hannibal took Imilce, the daughter of Castulo's chieftain, as his wife, holding the silver mountain firmly through a sacred marriage. It was the endless flow of silver from Castulo that forged the war god's iron flood of Balearic slingers, Gallic swordsmen and Numidian cavalry.

Variants.Content: The mines of Castulo pour out the lifeblood of the empire. As long as the furnaces of the Sierra Morena burn day and night, General Hannibal can recruit the bravest mercenaries on any battlefield!

The Barcid family traded a marriage for our silver mountain and our young men. Tens of thousands of tribal miners bleed and sweat in pitch-dark shafts, and all they get in return is a foreigner's coins.
The moment Scipio's army took Castulo, Hannibal's purse was tied shut for good. Without its silver mines, Carthage's mercenary army is nothing but loose sand!
